title: Nia and Pebble's Ice House Secret
markdown:
Once upon a time, nestled among the whispering pine trees, there was a super cozy summer house. And who lived there? Nia the squirrel. Nia was a busy little thing, with fur the colour of perfectly toasted hazelnuts and eyes that sparkled like shiny dewdrops. Her nest was so neat and tidy you could see your reflection in the polished acorn caps. She had collections of the most wonderful treasures: dewdrops that sparkled like tiny diamonds on spiderwebs, shiny bits of rock that winked like fallen stars, and smooth round pebbles that the rain had tumbled until they gleamed. She arranged them all in perfect little rows. But — and this is a big bushy-tailed but — Nia sometimes felt a tiny bit too organised. A little bit too safe. She secretly wished for a tiny spark of thrill.

Now, just a short scuttle away, down by the sparkling blue sea, lived Pebble the shore crab. Pebble was a cheerful lime-green fellow, his shell looking as if it had been painted by the waves themselves. He loved scuttling sideways, which is what crabs do, and he had a special talent for finding the smoothest stones on the beach. He’d arrange them in neat little circles by his favourite sun-warmed rock, like a collection of silent stony friends. Every day Pebble would arrange his stones, humming a little clicky-clacky tune. But — and this is the other half of the but — Pebble sometimes felt a tiny bit too safe. A little bit too predictable. He wished for a little bit of adventure.

Every single day, Nia would polish her treasures until they shone brighter than a firefly, and Pebble would arrange his stones, humming his little tune.

Until one day — whoosh. A strange chilly puff of air swirled around the summer house. It wasn’t the usual warm summer breeze that smelled of pine needles and sun-baked earth. This was different. This was cold. It tickled Nia’s nose and made her whiskers twitch. “Brrr. That’s a funny sneeze, summer,” she chittered, tiny paws rubbing together.

Down by the shore, Pebble felt it too. A shiver, like a tiny wave, ran through his many legs. He pulled his claws closer to his lime-green body. “Ooooh, that’s a bit nippy,” he clicked, peeking out from under his perfectly arranged stones. This mysterious cold puff seemed to be coming from under the cozy summer house, as if the house were taking a strange cold breath. Nia’s whiskers twitched with curiosity. A little tremor rippled through them. A little bit spooky, she thought, and her organised heart did a little flip-flop.

Because of that, Nia, who was usually all about neatness but secretly a tad adventurous, decided she had to know what was making that chilly breath. She scurried down from her nest, her heart thumping like a tiny drum. “Hello?” she squeaked, her voice a little wobbly, like a loose acorn.

Pebble, who had scampered out from his rock collection to get a better look, saw Nia standing there, looking very determined but also a tiny bit nervous. He knew that feeling in his shell. If Nia was going on an adventure, he could not just scuttle away and hide behind a seashell. “Wait for me, Nia,” he called, and with a series of rapid sideways hops he joined her. He felt a funny flutter in his shell, like a tiny butterfly trying to get out.

Together they tiptoed to the side of the summer house where the cold puff was strongest. The cold air hit them like an icy wave. It tickled Nia’s nose with the smell of old snow and damp earth, felt rough and dry on her fur, and whispered a hollow whoosh that made her shiver right down to her toes. “It smells clean. And old. Like a forgotten dream,” she whispered. Pebble tapped the wooden floorboards with his claw, listening. “And it sounds hollow. Like an empty treasure chest.”

Nia, with a mighty heave for a squirrel, pushed against a loose floorboard. It creaked and groaned, and then — pop — it lifted just enough for her to peer underneath. A rush of frosty air blasted out, carrying a scent like a freezer bag left open too long. Nia’s eyes widened. She held her breath.

Because of that, they discovered a dark opening, and from it poured that amazing frosty breath. It wasn’t a monster. It wasn’t a scary ghost. Nia, taking a deep warm breath, wriggled down into the opening. Pebble, with a brave click of his claws, followed right behind, his little legs going faster than they ever had before. The chilly air swirled around him like a gentle cold hug.

They landed with a soft thud on a floor that felt smooth and surprisingly icy. Inside, the air was so cold it bit at their noses, tasted like pure clean water on their tongues, and made their breath puff out in little white clouds. The ice walls gleamed like polished glass, felt slick and impossibly smooth when they dared to touch, and hummed with a low, almost silent chill. It was an underground ice house, like the ones people used long ago to keep winter’s ice frozen all the way through the hot summer. The breathing they felt was just the cool air gently escaping from this secret frosty place.

“Wowee,” chittered Nia, eyes wide. “It’s like a secret winter cave right under our feet.”

Because of that, Nia and Pebble understood. The scary cold breath wasn’t scary at all. It was just the whisper of old ice, a gentle reminder of snowy days in the middle of summer. Nia felt a thrill, not of fright, but of exciting discovery. It felt way, way better than just being perfectly organised. Pebble looked at Nia, his little crab eyes twinkling. A new sense of confidence bloomed in his shell, warmer than the sunniest rock.

Until finally they sat together in the cool quiet of the ice house, listening to the gentle sigh of the ice. Nia carefully picked out one of her shiniest, most perfectly round pebbles. Then, with a very careful movement, Pebble placed one of his smoothest greyest stones right next to it. A special secret shared between two very different friends. The cold was no longer strange or spooky. It was a fascinating secret they now both knew.

Ever since then, Nia’s nest had one extra special, cool-feeling stone: a smooth grey stone, a perfect souvenir from their underground adventure. And Pebble had a brand new story to scuttle about along the beach, a tale about the day he and his friend Nia discovered the amazing Whispering Ice House. And sometimes, when the summer sun was extra hot, they’d sneak down for a quick cool breath, two friends sharing their most surprising, and most heartwarming, secret.
